observations: Torah #117 teaches about the spiritual mechanism by which entering kedusha gevohah (high holiness) triggers the yetzer hara. The causal chain is: (1) a person enters kedusha (e.g., draws close to the true tzaddik); (2) this causes matzdik et atzmo milemata (self-justification from below); (3) which triggers matzdikin alav hadin milemala (strict judgment from above, per Taanis 8); (4) the dinim chain down (hishtalshelus hadinim); (5) from which the yetzer hara is generated (per LM1 #72). Additionally, the Rebbe explains that hidden tuma (tuma temuna) is expelled through proximity to kedusha, which is actually beneficial — once revealed, it can be rectified. The biblical paradigm is Avraham -> Yishmael -> Yitzchak and Yitzchak -> Esav -> Yaakov: the zuhama (spiritual pollution) must exit first. Key concepts: kedusha, kitrug/dinim, yetzer hara, mikre bilti tahor, tuma temuna, Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur, hishtalshelus hadinim, Avraham/Yishmael, Yitzchak/Esav/Yaakov. All connections are causal (eitza-type), not parallel-aspect (bechina-type). No formal bechina statements exist in this text, so no bechina-based packages can be formed.
